text:
Connor Brown has become a bigger part of the Devils since Anthony Mantha went down, up to about 17 minutes a night from 14, and he has answered with six goals and 11 points in 15 games. One of those goals, against Washington, looked an awful lot like a kick, and the Capitals said so. He also had three points that night.

The shooting is the part to treat carefully. Six goals on 3.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances) is a 27% rate, against 16% last season, and the Devils have scored a few more goals than their chances with him on. The bigger concern is five on five: New Jersey takes 46% of the expected goals with him out there, almost 12 points worse than without him, on a team that usually dominates. He is a useful veteran with a nice touch on the royal-road pass, 19% of his setups by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Our range has him around 19 goals. Expect the goals to slow even if the minutes stay.
